title: Unprovability of polynomial circuit upper bounds in \(S_2^1\)
formal:
Is the following unconditional unprovability statement true?
\[\forall k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\ \exists\eta\ \forall c\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}:\qquad S_2^1\nvdash\operatorname{UB}_{c,k}[\eta].\]
Here \(\eta(x,y)\) must be a \(\Sigma_1^b\) formula for which \(S_2^1\) proves that every \(x\) has exactly one output \(y\). It therefore represents a polynomial-time function. The sentence \(\operatorname{UB}_{c,k}[\eta]\), defined below with explicit coding, asserts that the predicate “the output is nonzero” has exact Boolean circuits of description size at most \(c n^k\) on every positive input length \(n\).

For each fixed exponent, the same represented function must resist provability for every fixed coefficient. The question concerns what this formal theory can prove; it does not ask directly for a circuit lower bound in the standard natural numbers or for unprovability of all possible upper bounds for one fixed function.
why: Circuit upper bounds assert that small nonuniform computations exist, even when no efficient method for finding them is supplied. This question asks whether a theory designed to formalize polynomial-time reasoning can certify fixed-polynomial circuit bounds for every polynomial-time predicate. A positive result would expose an unconditional limitation on the power of such proofs without requiring the corresponding unconditional circuit separation.

sentences: For each fixed polynomial exponent, the question asks for a polynomial-time predicate whose corresponding circuit upper bounds cannot be proved in S-two-one.
The same predicate must resist every fixed multiplicative coefficient in that exponent.
Its function representation, the arithmetic theory, circuit encoding and length quantifiers are explicitly specified.
The conclusion is nonprovability of upper bounds, not an asserted standard-model circuit lower bound.
Recent weaker-theory results and EXP consistency results leave this particular target open in the checked sources.

definitions:
Use classical first-order logic with equality and the one-sorted language \(L=\{0,1,+,\cdot,H,\ell,\#,\le\}\). Here \(H\) and \(\ell\) are unary, \(+\), \(\cdot\), \(\#\) are binary, and \(\le\) is a binary predicate. Terms are the finite expressions formed from variables, these constants and these function symbols. Atomic formulas are equalities or inequalities between terms. The logical operations are negation, conjunction, disjunction and first-order universal/existential quantification; implication and equivalence abbreviate their usual Boolean expansions. The successor notation \(Sx\) abbreviates \(x+1\), \(2\) abbreviates \(1+1\), and \(2x\) means \(2\cdot x\).

The intended standard structure has domain \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,\ldots\}\), its usual addition, multiplication and order, \(H(x)=\lfloor x/2\rfloor\), \(\ell(0)=0\), \(\ell(x)=\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor+1\) for \(x>0\), and \(x\#y=2^{\ell(x)\ell(y)}\). This interpretation explains the symbols; the theory's nonlogical axioms are exactly the following finite BASIC list and the specified induction scheme, rather than all sentences true in this standard structure. Every free variable in the following displays is universally quantified.

The order and successor axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
a\le b\ \to\ a\le b+1,\qquad a\ne a+1,\qquad 0\le a,\\
(a\le b\land a\ne b)\ \to\ a+1\le b,\qquad a\ne0\ \to\ 2a\ne0,\\
a\le b\lor b\le a,\qquad (a\le b\land b\le a)\ \to\ a=b,\\
(a\le b\land b\le c)\ \to\ a\le c,\qquad a\le a+b,\\
(a\le b\land a\ne b)\ \to\ (2a+1\le2b\land 2a+1\ne2b).
\end{gathered}\]
The addition and multiplication axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
a+b=b+a,\qquad a+0=a,\qquad a+(b+1)=(a+b)+1,\\
(a+b)+c=a+(b+c),\qquad a+b\le a+c\ \to\ b\le c,\\
a\cdot0=0,\qquad a\cdot(b+1)=a\cdot b+a,\qquad a\cdot b=b\cdot a,\\
a\cdot(b+c)=(a\cdot b)+(a\cdot c),\\
1\le a\ \to\ ((a\cdot b\le a\cdot c)\leftrightarrow(b\le c)).
\end{gathered}\]
The length, halving and smash axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
\ell(0)=0,\qquad \ell(1)=1,\qquad a\le b\ \to\ \ell(a)\le\ell(b),\\
a\ne0\ \to\ (\ell(2a)=\ell(a)+1\land\ell(2a+1)=\ell(a)+1),\\
\ell(a\#b)=\ell(a)\cdot\ell(b)+1,\qquad 0\#a=1,\\
a\ne0\ \to\ (1\#(2a)=2(1\#a)\land1\#(2a+1)=2(1\#a)),\\
a\#b=b\#a,\qquad \ell(a)=\ell(b)\ \to\ a\#c=b\#c,\\
\ell(a)=\ell(b)+\ell(c)\ \to\ a\#d=(b\#d)\cdot(c\#d),\\
a\ne0\ \to\ \ell(a)=\ell(H(a))+1,\\
a=H(b)\ \leftrightarrow\ (2a=b\lor2a+1=b).
\end{gathered}\]
These are the 32 axioms in Krajíček's Definition 5.2.1, regrouped by operation, with \(H\) and \(\ell\) replacing the printed halving and length notation. No sequence function or oracle predicate is added.

For a term \(t\) not containing \(y\), write \(\exists y\le t\,\psi\) for \(\exists y(y\le t\land\psi)\), and \(\forall y\le t\,\psi\) for \(\forall y(y\le t\to\psi)\). These are bounded quantifiers. They are sharply bounded when the bound is explicitly \(\ell(t)\). The bound may contain other free variables. Let \(\Sigma_0^b=\Pi_0^b\) be all formulas built from atomic formulas using Boolean operations and only sharply bounded quantifiers. Recursively, \(\Sigma_{r+1}^b,\Pi_{r+1}^b\) are the smallest pair of classes satisfying: both contain \(\Sigma_r^b\cup\Pi_r^b\); both are closed under conjunction, disjunction and both sharply bounded quantifiers; \(\Sigma_{r+1}^b\) is closed under bounded existential quantification; \(\Pi_{r+1}^b\) is closed under bounded universal quantification; and negation sends either class into the other. These are the full formula classes, allowing sharply bounded quantifiers inside as well as outside the other quantifiers, rather than only a strict prenex fragment.

For a set \(T\) of closed axioms, \(T\vdash\theta\) means that the closed sentence \(\theta\) has a finite proof in classical first-order logic with equality from those axioms. Equivalently, every nonempty \(L\)-structure satisfying all axioms of \(T\) satisfies \(\theta\). This equivalence is first-order completeness; structures in this characterization are not restricted to the standard natural numbers. There is no bound on proof length. Equality of theories here means equality of their deductive closures in the same language.

The theory \(S_2^1\) has BASIC and the universal closure over the parameter variables \(\vec a\) of
\[\bigl(\varphi(0,\vec a)\land\forall x(\varphi(H(x),\vec a)\to\varphi(x,\vec a))\bigr)\ \to\ \forall x\,\varphi(x,\vec a)\]
for every \(\Sigma_1^b\) formula \(\varphi\). This is polynomial induction, with halving in the hypothesis; it is not unrestricted successor induction for these formulas.

To specify the polynomial-time predicate without leaving its formal representation implicit, let \(\eta(x,y)\) range over \(\Sigma_1^b\) formulas whose only free variables are among \(x,y\) and for which
\[S_2^1\vdash\forall x\,\exists y\bigl(\eta(x,y)\land\forall z(\eta(x,z)\to z=y)\bigr).\]
Thus the theory proves that \(\eta\) defines one total number-valued function. The associated language consists of numbers whose unique output is nonzero. By the definability/witnessing characterization of \(S_2^1\), these provably total \(\Sigma_1^b\) graphs represent polynomial-time functions. This is a base-language presentation of the source's polynomial-time function symbols in a conservative definitional extension. The formula \(\eta\), rather than just its extension in the standard natural numbers, is part of the witness being quantified over.

Here is an explicit arithmetic encoding of the circuits used in the upper-bound sentence. An \(n\)-input circuit has constants at nodes zero and one, inputs at nodes \(2,\ldots,n+1\), and \(g\ge0\) computational nodes \(n+2,\ldots,n+g+1\) in evaluation order. Each computational node has a two-bit operation tag: zero is AND, one OR, two NOT of the first predecessor, and three a copy of the first predecessor. It also has two predecessor indices, both less than its own index; the second is ignored for the last two tags. The output is any node. Shared values and unrestricted depth are allowed, with exact correctness on all inputs. Copy gates are only a serialization convenience and can be removed; this is an ordinary bounded-fan-in Boolean model.

Let \(w=\ell(n+g+2)\), \(q=2+2w\), and \(d=gq+w\). The circuit number \(C\) has binary length \(d+1\); its highest bit is a delimiter. In the lower bits, counted from position zero at the least significant bit, gate \(i\in\{0,\ldots,g-1\}\) has its tag at positions \(iq,iq+1\), first predecessor in the next \(w\) bits, and second predecessor in the next \(w\) bits. The output index occupies the \(w\) bits starting at \(gq\). A valid encoding has both predecessors below \(n+2+i\) and output below \(n+g+2\). Denote these conditions by \(\operatorname{Valid}(n,g,C)\). The description size charged in the sentence is \(\ell(C)+\ell(g)\); the input length is supplied separately. Thus the measure is a binary description length, not an unannounced change to an exact gate-count bound.

All bit and field operations in this description have the following fixed bounded-arithmetic expansion. For \(X\ge1\), define \(\operatorname{Field}(X,a,b,v)\) by the existence of \(z,t,u,r,s\), all at most \(X+(1\#X)+1\), such that
\[\begin{gathered}
z=1\#H(z),\quad \ell(z)=a+1,\quad t=1\#H(t),\quad \ell(t)=b+1,\\
X=uz+r,\quad r<z,\quad u=st+v,\quad v<t.
\end{gathered}\]
Here \(a\) is the starting position, \(b\ge1\) is field width, and \(u< v\) abbreviates \(u\le v\land u\ne v\). The equations select \(z=2^a\) and \(t=2^b\). Define \(\operatorname{Bit}(X,a,e)\), for \(e\in\{0,1\}\), as
\[(\ell(X)\le a\land e=0)\ \lor\ (a<\ell(X)\land\operatorname{Field}(X,a,1,e)).\]
This also defines the padded zero bits of \(X=0\). In \(\operatorname{Valid}\), each extracted tag or index is a bounded existential variable at most \(n+g+4\); gate checks are quantified over \(i<g\). These conventions expand validity into one definite arithmetic formula.

Define \(\operatorname{Eval}(N,n,g,C,x)\) to assert that the encoded circuit outputs one on the \(n\)-bit, zero-padded representation of \(x\). Its arithmetic expansion is: validity holds and there exists an integer
\[V\le (N\#N)\cdot(C\#C)\]
whose bits at node indices give a correct evaluation, with output bit one. Bits zero and one of \(V\) equal zero and one respectively; for each \(r<n\), bit \(r+2\) of \(V\) equals bit \(r\) of \(x\); and for each \(i<g\), the bit at \(n+2+i\) is the Boolean operation indicated by the tag applied to the predecessor bits. All field and bit occurrences use the preceding formulas, with Boolean auxiliary variables bounded by one and extracted indices bounded by \(n+g+4\). The four Boolean operations are specified by their truth tables. The output index is extracted from its field and its \(V\)-bit must be one. The quantifiers over nodes and gates are bounded by \(n\) and \(g\). Since validity implies \(g\le\ell(C)\) and \(n=\ell(N)\ge1\), the displayed bound is ample for the finite evaluation vector. This description fixes the formula through bounded quantifiers and Boolean combinations, and introduces no extra axioms about an opaque evaluator.

For fixed positive integers \(c,k\), let \(\operatorname{UB}_{c,k}[\eta]\) be the following closed \(L\)-sentence, with the defined predicates expanded:
\[\begin{split}
\forall N\ge1\ \exists g\ \exists C\ \bigl(&\operatorname{Valid}(n,g,C)\land\ell(C)+\ell(g)\le c\,n^k\\
&\land\forall x\ \forall y\bigl((\ell(x)\le n\land\eta(x,y))\to
(\operatorname{Eval}(N,n,g,C,x)\leftrightarrow y\ne0)\bigr)\bigr),
\end{split}\]
where every \(n\) abbreviates \(\ell(N)\). The fixed numeral \(c\) and fixed power \(n^k\) are expanded using multiplication. This is the source's Log convention: lengths come from the length of an arbitrarily quantified number, instead of treating their unary encodings as separately available objects. Zero input length is omitted. The quantifier \(\ell(x)\le n\) permits leading-zero padding; the represented function is a function of the number \(x\), exactly as in the source's unary function-symbol formulation.

The choices of \(k\), \(\eta\) and \(c\) in the main question are external standard integers/formulas. For each fixed exponent, one formula must work against every coefficient. The required conclusion is absence of any finite proof of each displayed upper-bound sentence, not that the theory proves its negation. The description encoding above makes a routine circuit serialization explicit; it is not a claim that the source printed this exact bit layout. Polynomially related standard circuit encodings yield the same all-exponents unprovability target after a fixed change of exponent and coefficient. No single EXP language or unproved complexity assumption substitutes for a provably total polynomial-time graph.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed metamathematical statement. A positive answer must, for every standard exponent \(k\ge1\), establish a permitted formula \(\eta\) with its \(S_2^1\)-provable totality and uniqueness and prove that no finite \(S_2^1\) proof of \(\operatorname{UB}_{c,k}[\eta]\) exists for any standard coefficient \(c\ge1\). A negative answer must establish an exponent \(k\) such that every permitted \(\eta\) has some coefficient \(c\) for which the corresponding upper-bound sentence is provable. The coefficient and proof may depend on \(\eta\). Nonprovability for a weaker theory, an EXP computation, one proposed proof, or one coefficient alone is insufficient. No unproved complexity hypothesis is part of the target.

context_blocks.text: The source formulates the question through polynomial-time function symbols and upper-bound sentences with an external size coefficient. The card uses their provably total bounded-arithmetic graph presentation and supplies an explicit circuit encoding, so that function representation and length quantifiers are part of the statement.

The 2025 survey records unconditional unprovability of fixed-polynomial circuit upper bounds in Cook’s weaker theory PV. It separately asks whether the analogous conclusion holds for the stronger polynomial-induction theory used here.

The February 2026 preprint extends upper-bound unprovability to \(PV_1+BB(\Sigma_1^b)\). Its Section 1.2.5 and Figure 2 explicitly leave the \(S_2^1\) case open. This is a claimed improvement of the theory for which unprovability is known, with the remaining gap preserved.

The April 2026 preprint establishes consistency of \(S_2^1\) with a formalized superpolynomial circuit lower bound for EXP. Its exponential-time computation and sentence conventions differ from the polynomial-time, fixed-exponent question here; its main theorem is not recorded as a resolution of this card.
